title: ML Drift: Next-Gen GPU AI/ML Inference at the Edge
key_facts: Google's AI Edge team released ML Drift as open source under the Apache 2.0 licence.
It is a GPU engine for running AI models on devices, across OpenGL ES, OpenCL, Metal and WebGPU, and is the core GPU engine in LiteRT.
It replaces the older TensorFlow Lite GPU delegate, which will no longer get new feature updates.
Google says it already runs on millions of devices daily, in Chrome, YouTube Shorts, Photos, Meet and AI Edge Gallery.
Google reports up to 40% lower average frame delay in YouTube Shorts effects, and up to 30% faster Adobe Lightroom and Photoshop AI features on mobile.
Windows and Linux support are desktop previews; in Gemma tests it uses up to 12% less memory than other frameworks, per Google.
It adds 5D tensor support and a guide so coding agents can write custom GPU shaders.
quote_evidence: ML Drift is already running in production across millions of devices daily, powering key features across Google's ecosystem, including Chrome, YouTube Shorts, Photos, Meet, and the recently launched AI Edge Gallery.
With the launch of ML Drift, the legacy TFLite GPU delegate will no longer receive new feature updates.
why_it_matters_hint: One open engine for on-device AI across many chips; performance numbers are Google's own.
notes: Official Google post, read in full except the benchmark charts. All figures are Google's own claims.
